Applicable summary text:
**Attrition:** Simultaneously roll one die for each held office card. Add one per fatigue on that card; Chairman also adds one. Modified 1–2: nothing; 3–4: add fatigue; 5+: retire. Move retiree to Pensioners, flip card into Vacant Offices, return its fatigue to supply. Commanders have no office card and do not roll normal office attrition.

**Region Loss:** Commander returns half their family's trophies rounded up, then Commander member returns to supply. Roll once per officer in associated Army: each 6 removes that officer. Eliminate Governor: return office card to unused stack, fatigue and member to supplies. Remove Governor overlay, partially built Company ship and unrest. Restore dome with one tower (or Foreign Invasion's specified strength) and appropriate invasion flag. Return control token to its region with **the £ loot side DOWN and the region-symbol side UP**. Future conquest gets no loot modifier; region loses its Presidency association. An Invasion Crisis closes all its orders, or Cascades if already closed; Rebellion/Foreign Invasion already close them. Standing loss equals number of regions lost **so far this turn**, including this one: first -1, second additional -2, etc. If this causes failure, finish Events in India before Final Scoring. **Losing one region does not automatically lose any other Company region: resolve each other attack and its defense separately.**

- **Form a firm — only if you currently manage none:** return one eligible Company share to supply or flip workshop to invested side. **Flip your family board to its firm-charter side**, then place a family member as first firm share, set value cube to leftmost track space and take £5 from bank into the London treasury.
- **Invest:** With manager's consent, same Company-share/workshop contribution creates one firm share and £5 bank to London. Up to ten firm shares; further investments still contribute £5 but create no shares. Cannot use Chairman share. Cannot use Company shares at all when Standing and/or Debt on lined space. Cannot use shares created this turn, even after trading them away. Invested workshops never return to uninvested: no bonus or Company-failure VP; they remain invested even if firm fails.
- **Ships:** A firm may fit a ship from **its own OR ANOTHER PLAYER'S shipyard**, but **must have that shipyard owner's consent**. Pay **£3 FROM the firm's London treasury TO the BANK**. May buy player-owned ship already in Company with owner's consent: unfatigued £3, fatigued £2, paid into Shipping treasury. Firms cannot acquire Company or extra ships.
- **Hostile takeover:** Only a player who **manages NO firm at all** may initiate one; managing a different firm also makes you ineligible. Obtain consent of holders of a majority of the target's shares, then move firm's ships, money and shares to own charter, copy both cube positions; former manager returns cubes and flips board to family side.
- **Merger:** Managers negotiate with **every shareholder's consent**. Highest-value firm is primary; if tied, players choose among tied. Transfer all secondary shares, ships and treasury funds to primary; secondary boards return to family sides. Players may negotiate share transfers. **If the primary would exceed ten shares, RETURN the excess shares to their OWNERS' SUPPLIES, with those owners' consent.** Entire agreement is one binding immediate transfer. Primary's value/dividend track remains the continuing firm's track.
- **Voluntary dissolution:** All shareholders must consent. Apply the same dissolution procedure as an insolvent firm: **shares go to Debtor's Prison (each −1 VP), ships return to their matching shipyards, and the charter flips to its family side. Workshops remain invested for the rest of the game.**

Applicable summary text:
**Retirements:** Starting with the Chairman (former Chairman if vacant), clockwise, each player may retire each pensioner to a prize. Pay its printed cost, move the member to the prize and gain printed VP. Set actual spending aside until London Season ends to establish display-selection order, then pay bank. Prizes may incur upkeep and window taxes. Unused pensioners do not remain for another turn.

**Special retirement:** Each shareholder may make one additional retirement per London Season from supply rather than Pensioners, irrespective of number of firms owned. **Actual cash spent after spouse discounts** cannot exceed the **highest total dividend marker** of any firm they own a share in; the printed prize cost may exceed that marker when discounts cover the difference. No retirement from a firm whose marker is absent or zero. Spouse discounts can allow a higher printed-cost prize; retirement otherwise normal, including prestige eligibility. At start of Final Scoring, score firms then allow one special retirement regardless of Company success/failure, before normal final-scoring steps; no display cards in Final Scoring.

**Prestige:** Players who completed at least one pensioner retirement **or an eligible firm special retirement during this London Season** must each take or discard one display card, in descending actual total retirement spending. A firm special retirement uses a supply member instead of a pensioner but otherwise counts as a normal retirement for this selection; each eligible player still selects only one card. Ties: most total windows, including new prizes, then clockwise from PM. Acting player may peek at display blackmails. **Do not replace a chosen/discarded card during selection. If the display becomes empty, immediately skip every remaining eligible player.** Finish the display step by **discarding all remaining cards and refilling exactly three: prestige faceup, blackmail facedown, even if nobody took a card**. Return all remaining Pensioners to their supplies.

| Enlist Writer | Place a member in any Presidency's Writers box. With at least four vacant offices, place one additional writer **once this turn**, so a doubled Writer action can place three total. |

**Successful Trade capacity is one order per ship in this Presidency's sea zone. Trade does not exhaust ships.** Fill as many orders as possible within declared regions. First writer goes to home port. Every later order must extend the connected route filled during this same Presidency's Trade. **Writers from another Presidency cannot extend this route**, even when adjacent. **Writers do not limit capacity: use all available writers, then continue filling with filled-order tokens for the remaining ships.** Those tokens continue this Trade's own route. No President may fill another President's home region, even if its office vacant. Increase Balance by each order's printed value, **or half rounded down if a firm already filled it this turn under Deregulation**. President earns bank £1 per order; writer owners earn £1 per writer placed. Separate adjacent writers from different Presidencies with dividers for correct return at Refresh.

Fill vacant offices in ascending number on their card backs. The designated hirer chooses a candidate and moves that member into the office; its owner gets the card. When promoting an officeholder, transfer its fatigue to the new card and insert its old card, vacant, into ascending hiring order. If no candidate exists, or the hirer is vacant, skip the office; it stays vacant and takes no actions, including hiring.

Applicable summary text:
- **Form a firm — only if you currently manage none:** return one eligible Company share to supply or flip workshop to invested side. **Flip your family board to its firm-charter side**, then place a family member as first firm share, set value cube to leftmost track space and take £5 from bank into the London treasury.
- **Invest:** With manager's consent, same Company-share/workshop contribution creates one firm share and £5 bank to London. Up to ten firm shares; further investments still contribute £5 but create no shares. Cannot use Chairman share. Cannot use Company shares at all when Standing and/or Debt on lined space. Cannot use shares created this turn, even after trading them away. Invested workshops never return to uninvested: no bonus or Company-failure VP; they remain invested even if firm fails.
- **Ships:** A firm may fit a ship from **its own OR ANOTHER PLAYER'S shipyard**, but **must have that shipyard owner's consent**. Pay **£3 FROM the firm's London treasury TO the BANK**. May buy player-owned ship already in Company with owner's consent: unfatigued £3, fatigued £2, paid into Shipping treasury. Firms cannot acquire Company or extra ships.
- **Hostile takeover:** Only a player who **manages NO firm at all** may initiate one; managing a different firm also makes you ineligible. Obtain consent of holders of a majority of the target's shares, then move firm's ships, money and shares to own charter, copy both cube positions; former manager returns cubes and flips board to family side.
- **Merger:** Managers negotiate with **every shareholder's consent**. Highest-value firm is primary; if tied, players choose among tied. Transfer all secondary shares, ships and treasury funds to primary; secondary boards return to family sides. Players may negotiate share transfers. **If the primary would exceed ten shares, RETURN the excess shares to their OWNERS' SUPPLIES, with those owners' consent.** Entire agreement is one binding immediate transfer. Primary's value/dividend track remains the continuing firm's track.
- **Voluntary dissolution:** All shareholders must consent. Apply the same dissolution procedure as an insolvent firm: **shares go to Debtor's Prison (each −1 VP), ships return to their matching shipyards, and the charter flips to its family side. Workshops remain invested for the rest of the game.**

If unable to pay, dissolve unless rescued. Dissolution: shares to Debtor's Prison (each -1 VP), ships back to shipyards, charter back to family side; workshops remain invested. Emergency investments follow normal Company-share/workshop rules, even when ten-share cap prevents more shares: pay expenses, lose any remaining cash, lower Value one space per emergency investment. Alternatively make an **emergency negotiated merger with only ONE other firm**. The normal merger procedure still applies, including **every involved shareholder's consent**. The other firm must first pay its own expenses if not already paid, then cover the endangered firm's unpaid expenses.

Applicable summary text:
May make repeated Special Envoy checks: £1 treasury cash per die, no penalty. Success either opens one closed order in a **non-Company** region, or opens China: place Superintendent overlay/card and Chairman hires writer immediately. Created by successful envoy **or** Envoy to China law; **in either case the Chairman immediately hires any writer**. Its treasury holds ships, not cash. Shipping and Director of Trade may send ships here like any sea zone. They count Eastern for expenses, events, storms and laws. After Bengal, may attempt China Trade **only ONCE, including a failed attempt: no retry**. Roll one die per ship. **Without an export icon in Company-controlled regions, do not attempt China Trade at all.**

**Foreign Invasion and unrest:** Cole Wehrle clarified on April 30, 2023 that unrest does **not** add to a Foreign Invasion's primary attack strength or determine its resulting tower levels. Use the ordinary die roll for both attack strength and halving to create towers; the event still uses the Company-defense procedure and its secondary unrest attacks. Do not apply the normal primary Crisis's added unrest to this special event. [Designer ruling](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2962161/article/42192767#42192767). **On a successful Foreign Invasion, close all orders in the target region once; if they are already all closed, Cascade instead.** Region Loss does not close them a second time: its additional closure is only for a normal Invasion Crisis.

Firm managers control firms; firm shares can be traded like Company shares. A firm has two treasuries: **London** receives the bank's £5 per investment and pays for ship acquisition, trade bids and expenses; **India** receives trade and pays dividends/expenses. **Investment cash always comes FROM the BANK TO London. London cash cannot buy new equity shares; creating shares requires a Company-share or workshop contribution.** **Family cash cannot be transferred into or out of firm treasuries.** Only specified investment, payout and expense procedures move it.

- **Form a firm — only if you currently manage none:** return one eligible Company share to supply or flip workshop to invested side. **Flip your family board to its firm-charter side**, then place a family member as first firm share, set value cube to leftmost track space and take £5 from bank into the London treasury.
- **Invest:** With manager's consent, same Company-share/workshop contribution creates one firm share and £5 bank to London. Up to ten firm shares; further investments still contribute £5 but create no shares. Cannot use Chairman share. Cannot use Company shares at all when Standing and/or Debt on lined space. Cannot use shares created this turn, even after trading them away. Invested workshops never return to uninvested: no bonus or Company-failure VP; they remain invested even if firm fails.
- **Ships:** A firm may fit a ship from **its own OR ANOTHER PLAYER'S shipyard**, but **must have that shipyard owner's consent**. Pay **£3 FROM the firm's London treasury TO the BANK**. May buy player-owned ship already in Company with owner's consent: unfatigued £3, fatigued £2, paid into Shipping treasury. Firms cannot acquire Company or extra ships.
- **Hostile takeover:** Only a player who **manages NO firm at all** may initiate one; managing a different firm also makes you ineligible. Obtain consent of holders of a majority of the target's shares, then move firm's ships, money and shares to own charter, copy both cube positions; former manager returns cubes and flips board to family side.

Transfer all secondary shares, ships and treasury funds to primary; secondary boards return to family sides. Players may negotiate share transfers. **If the primary would exceed ten shares, RETURN the excess shares to their OWNERS' SUPPLIES, with those owners' consent.** Entire agreement is one binding immediate transfer. Primary's value/dividend track remains the continuing firm's track.

Up to ten firm shares; further investments still contribute £5 but create no shares. Cannot use Chairman share. Cannot use Company shares at all when Standing and/or Debt on lined space. Cannot use shares created this turn, even after trading them away. Invested workshops never return to uninvested: no bonus or Company-failure VP; they remain invested even if firm fails.
- **Ships:** A firm may fit a ship from **its own OR ANOTHER PLAYER'S shipyard**, but **must have that shipyard owner's consent**. Pay **£3 FROM the firm's London treasury TO the BANK**. May buy player-owned ship already in Company with owner's consent: unfatigued £3, fatigued £2, paid into Shipping treasury. Firms cannot acquire Company or extra ships.
- **Hostile takeover:** Only a player who **manages NO firm at all** may initiate one; managing a different firm also makes you ineligible. Obtain consent of holders of a majority of the target's shares, then move firm's ships, money and shares to own charter, copy both cube positions; former manager returns cubes and flips board to family side.
- **Merger:** Managers negotiate with **every shareholder's consent**. Highest-value firm is primary; if tied, players choose among tied. Transfer all secondary shares, ships and treasury funds to primary; secondary boards return to family sides. Players may negotiate share transfers. **If the primary would exceed ten shares, RETURN the excess shares to their OWNERS' SUPPLIES, with those owners' consent.** Entire agreement is one binding immediate transfer. Primary's value/dividend track remains the continuing firm's track.
- **Voluntary dissolution:** All shareholders must consent. Apply the same dissolution procedure as an insolvent firm: **shares go to Debtor's Prison (each −1 VP), ships return to their matching shipyards, and the charter flips to its family side. Workshops remain invested for the rest of the game.**

Applicable summary text:
**Foreign Invasion and unrest:** Cole Wehrle clarified on April 30, 2023 that unrest does **not** add to a Foreign Invasion's primary attack strength or determine its resulting tower levels. Use the ordinary die roll for both attack strength and halving to create towers; the event still uses the Company-defense procedure and its secondary unrest attacks. Do not apply the normal primary Crisis's added unrest to this special event. [Designer ruling](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2962161/article/42192767#42192767). **On a successful Foreign Invasion, close all orders in the target region once; if they are already all closed, Cascade instead.** Region Loss does not close them a second time: its additional closure is only for a normal Invasion Crisis.

- **Primary normal Crisis:** normal Invasion/Rebellion attack strength **plus unrest in its target region**.
- **Primary Foreign Invasion:** the ordinary attack die, with no added unrest (designer ruling in FAQ).
- **Every secondary Rebellion:** **only the number of unrest cubes in that secondary region**; no event modifier or empire strength.

**Region Loss:** Commander returns half their family's trophies rounded up, then Commander member returns to supply. Roll once per officer in associated Army: each 6 removes that officer. Eliminate Governor: return office card to unused stack, fatigue and member to supplies. Remove Governor overlay, partially built Company ship and unrest. Restore dome with one tower (or Foreign Invasion's specified strength) and appropriate invasion flag. Return control token to its region with **the £ loot side DOWN and the region-symbol side UP**. Future conquest gets no loot modifier; region loses its Presidency association. An Invasion Crisis closes all its orders, or Cascades if already closed; Rebellion/Foreign Invasion already close them. Standing loss equals number of regions lost **so far this turn**, including this one: first -1, second additional -2, etc. If this causes failure, finish Events in India before Final Scoring. **Losing one region does not automatically lose any other Company region: resolve each other attack and its defense separately.**

**India terminology:** A region's tower levels are its strength; the dome adds none. Orders are connected trading opportunities with printed revenue values; heavy outlines mark home ports. Closed orders cannot be filled. Sovereign regions have a dome without a flag or a capital/star flag; dominated regions have a small flag or no dome. An empire has one capital and at least one dominated region. **Whenever an empire loses its last dominated region, remove the surviving capital's starred flag: it is no longer an empire. This applies regardless of cause, including Rebellion or Company conquest of that last dominated region.** Presidencies are Bombay, Madras and Bengal, each with its own treasury, writers, fleet, Army and associated Company regions.

**Region Loss:** Commander returns half their family's trophies rounded up, then Commander member returns to supply. Roll once per officer in associated Army: each 6 removes that officer. Eliminate Governor: return office card to unused stack, fatigue and member to supplies. Remove Governor overlay, partially built Company ship and unrest. Restore dome with one tower (or Foreign Invasion's specified strength) and appropriate invasion flag. Return control token to its region with **the £ loot side DOWN and the region-symbol side UP**. Future conquest gets no loot modifier; region loses its Presidency association. An Invasion Crisis closes all its orders, or Cascades if already closed; Rebellion/Foreign Invasion already close them. Standing loss equals number of regions lost **so far this turn**, including this one: first -1, second additional -2, etc. If this causes failure, finish Events in India before Final Scoring. **Losing one region does not automatically lose any other Company region: resolve each other attack and its defense separately.**

**Choose the ordinary Crisis procedure from the Elephant:** Its **tail is the attacker/acting region; its head is the defender**. A sovereign actor (large capital flag or unflagged dome) causes **Invasion**. A dominated actor (small flag or no dome) causes **Rebellion against its sovereign**. If Elephant is wholly inside a Company region, resolve Rebellion against the Company. This classifier concerns ordinary Elephant-located Crisis events; Foreign Invasion uses its own location rule.

After expenses, manager may pay dividends **from India treasury only**. Each dividend pays £1 per firm share plus £1 manager. **Waiving a dividend requires BOTH the shareholder's choice and the MANAGER'S CONSENT**; shareholder consent alone is insufficient. With that consent, the shareholder may forgo payment for any number of shares on any dividend. Record **total actual cash paid out**, not per-share dividend, with dividend cube on Company Balance track. An active non-Hobnob firm paying none records zero; Hobnob retains prior marker. Sweep remaining India money into London. Firm ships face storms in strategy zone; Hobnob exempts them.

**Chairman election:** Former Chairman first announces **the number of shares needed for a pure majority** (more than half of current shares). Any shareholder may campaign; first candidate supported by players controlling that many shares wins. Move one winner's Company shares into Chairman slot and give title marker. It still counts as a share for dividends, majority and scoring, but cannot be traded or invested in firms. If no candidate gets support, former Chairman picks any shareholder including self; no Nepotism consent. If Court is empty, former Chairman automatically returns, placing a member from supply or, if necessary and possible, a prize (lose prize VP). If impossible, there is no Chairman.

**Special retirement:** Each shareholder may make one additional retirement per London Season from supply rather than Pensioners, irrespective of number of firms owned. **Actual cash spent after spouse discounts** cannot exceed the **highest total dividend marker** of any firm they own a share in; the printed prize cost may exceed that marker when discounts cover the difference. No retirement from a firm whose marker is absent or zero. Spouse discounts can allow a higher printed-cost prize; retirement otherwise normal, including prestige eligibility. At start of Final Scoring, score firms then allow one special retirement regardless of Company success/failure, before normal final-scoring steps; no display cards in Final Scoring.

The assigned Second Printing rulebook incorporates the core procedural corrections, including forced prize-piece reuse, empty Court, deployment boundaries, Region Loss and Elephant priority. Printed card corrections also specify: Mercantile/Diplomatic Connection reducing a check to zero dice means failure; Company Fraud is played at start of Revenue: roll one die per your officeholder, reduce Balance by twice the highest roll (minimum zero), and take cash from the bank equal to that actual Balance reduction; Public Demands Impeachment returns member to supply and office card to vacancies; Military Oversight demotes one Commander to an officer, then appoints a Commander from officers: **the SAME former Commander remains eligible to become COMMANDER again**. Applicable summary text:
After expenses, manager may pay dividends **from India treasury only**. Each dividend pays £1 per firm share plus £1 manager. **Waiving a dividend requires BOTH the shareholder's choice and the MANAGER'S CONSENT**; shareholder consent alone is insufficient. With that consent, the shareholder may forgo payment for any number of shares on any dividend. Record **total actual cash paid out**, not per-share dividend, with dividend cube on Company Balance track. An active non-Hobnob firm paying none records zero; Hobnob retains prior marker. Sweep remaining India money into London. Firm ships face storms in strategy zone; Hobnob exempts them.

- **Form a firm — only if you currently manage none:** return one eligible Company share to supply or flip workshop to invested side. **Flip your family board to its firm-charter side**, then place a family member as first firm share, set value cube to leftmost track space and take £5 from bank into the London treasury.
- **Invest:** With manager's consent, same Company-share/workshop contribution creates one firm share and £5 bank to London. Up to ten firm shares; further investments still contribute £5 but create no shares. Cannot use Chairman share. Cannot use Company shares at all when Standing and/or Debt on lined space. Cannot use shares created this turn, even after trading them away. Invested workshops never return to uninvested: no bonus or Company-failure VP; they remain invested even if firm fails.
- **Ships:** A firm may fit a ship from **its own OR ANOTHER PLAYER'S shipyard**, but **must have that shipyard owner's consent**. Pay **£3 FROM the firm's London treasury TO the BANK**. May buy player-owned ship already in Company with owner's consent: unfatigued £3, fatigued £2, paid into Shipping treasury. Firms cannot acquire Company or extra ships.
- **Hostile takeover:** Only a player who **manages NO firm at all** may initiate one; managing a different firm also makes you ineligible. Obtain consent of holders of a majority of the target's shares, then move firm's ships, money and shares to own charter, copy both cube positions; former manager returns cubes and flips board to family side.
- **Merger:** Managers negotiate with **every shareholder's consent**. Highest-value firm is primary; if tied, players choose among tied. Transfer all secondary shares, ships and treasury funds to primary; secondary boards return to family sides. Players may negotiate share transfers. **If the primary would exceed ten shares, RETURN the excess shares to their OWNERS' SUPPLIES, with those owners' consent.** Entire agreement is one binding immediate transfer. Primary's value/dividend track remains the continuing firm's track.
- **Voluntary dissolution:** All shareholders must consent. Apply the same dissolution procedure as an insolvent firm: **shares go to Debtor's Prison (each −1 VP), ships return to their matching shipyards, and the charter flips to its family side. Workshops remain invested for the rest of the game.**

1. **Expenses:** Reduce Balance £1 per existing Debt, each officer/regiment in an Army, and each ship in sea zones, including China. Exclude Commanders. If insufficient, take £5 emergency loans. Each loan advances Debt one **only while a track space remains**. **At maximum Debt, keep taking loans without advancing Debt any further.** Newly added emergency Debt causes no extra current-turn expense. After using emergency loans, set Balance to zero. One or two loans lower Standing one; three or more lower Standing two.
2. **Expectations:** Compare remaining Balance to the expectations under **current** Standing; if lower, lower Standing one.
3. **Dividends:** Chairman may pay any affordable number. Each dividend costs one cash per Company share; pay each owner £1 per share, including Chairman. If total cash paid as dividends is **strictly greater** than expectations, advance Standing one space.

Applicable summary text:
1. Check where your opportunity marker was **at phase start** (it begins off the board).
2. Choose a main family action: take it once, or **may take it twice if the marker already matched it**.
3. **Place/move the opportunity marker onto your chosen main action.**
4. After the main action, only the latest passed extra-action law may grant its extra action. This extra action is never doubled by the marker and never moves the marker.

| Family | Repeat last main action for double; vacancy writer bonus once; issue shares rightmost while Debt exists. |

If placing a family piece with none in supply, take one from any of your prizes and lose that prize's printed VP. This applies to firm-share creation too. If no family action is possible, take none and return opportunity marker to supply.
